newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria 1997 foreign debt payments at $992.2 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria 1997 foreign debt payments at $992.2 mln.

text.p: Bulgaria's foreign debt payments due this year amount to $992.2 million with the biggest burden concentrated in the first and fourth quarters, the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Monday.
"Foreign debt obligations including principal and interest due this year are estimated at $992.2 million," a BNB official who declined to named told Reuters.
Amounts are distributed in quarters as follows: $336.5 million due in the first quarter, $77.9 million due in the second quarter, $268.0 million in third quarter and $309.8 in fourth quarter.
Payments include dues to the Paris Club of government creditors and Brady Bond coupon payments totalling some $260 million of which $135.1 million was paid on January 28.

Bulgaria issued on July 28, 1994 three types of Brady bonds with a total par value of $5.1 billion as part of a restructuring deal on its $8.16 billion commercial debt to the London Club of creditor banks.

This year's debt service does not include payments on debt of around $1 billion owed to two COMECON banks, part of a former communist trade block which was disbanded six years ago, the central bank said.
Vice President of Salomon Brothers Emerging market research David Boren said that other preliminary estimates indicated that debt service burden will be over $1 billion, this year.

"The precise structure of the Bulgarian debt is complicated by the obligations owed to former COMECON banks and the ongoing debt-for-equity programme using Bulgarian Bradies," Boren told Reuters by telephone from London.
There was no record of how much Front Loaded Interest Reduction Bonds FLIRB's and Discount Bonds were used as means of payment in Bulgaria's privatisation programme so far.
